### Also covered by

Fong & Spivak, *Seven Sketches in Compositionality* §1.2.1, printed p. 7 (PDF p. 19), item `7sketches:1.2.1:def-subset` — the book's prose introduction of sets, subsets, the empty set and comprehension. Comprehension and membership of generalized elements are exactly this issue's obligation, and the in-tree side is if anything stronger (`Structure/SubobjectClassifier.v:187`'s `classifier_classifies` is a proven bijection with predicates, and `Instance/FinSet/Classifier.v:188`'s `fin_select_sat` computes). Two element-level clauses of the book's presentation are not reachable from the subobject reading: `Theory/Subobject.v:59`'s `sub_le` orders monos into a FIXED ambient object rather than relating two sets, and `Instance/Ens.v`'s homs are preimage equalities (`A = f⁻¹ B`) rather than inclusions.

- [ ] (from Seven Sketches §1.2.1) elementwise inclusion between two objects, `∀ x, x ∈ X → x ∈ Y`, and its comparison with the mono-level `sub_le`
- [ ] (from Seven Sketches §1.2.1) the empty set is a subobject of every object: the unique map `0 ~> x` is monic and names a least element of `SubObj x` (currently nothing in-tree says the initial map is monic; see also #247)

### Also covered by

Fong & Spivak, *Seven Sketches in Compositionality* §1.2.1, printed p. 12 (PDF p. 24), item `7sketches:1.2.1:example29` — elements of a set as functions out of the singleton, and evaluation as composition. Global elements as such are already in-tree data (`Structure/Constant.v:27`'s `constant (x : A) : 1 ~> constant_obj x`, `Tools/Represented.v:31`'s `convert : A → (1 ~> repr)`), and `Structure/Cartesian/Closed.v:389`'s `exp_one : x^1 ≅ x` holds in any cartesian closed category with a terminal object — at `Sets` it reads exactly as the book's identification, since `Instance/Sets/Cartesian/Closed.v:38` takes `exponent_obj x y` to be the hom-setoid `SetoidMorphism x y` and `Instance/Sets.v:248` is the singleton. Neither the instantiation nor the evaluation equation is written down.

- [ ] (from Seven Sketches §1.2.1) the external bijection `x ≅ (1 ~> x)` instantiated at `Sets` (and at `Coq`, noting that `Instance/Coq.v:167`'s `Coq_Closed` obligation spends `extensionality`)
- [ ] (from Seven Sketches §1.2.1) evaluation as composition for global elements: for `f : x ~> y` and a point `p : 1 ~> x`, `f ∘ p` is the point naming `f p` — stated generally, not only inside `Tools/Abstraction.v`'s AST-relative `rel` (`:52`, `:82`)

### Also covered by

Fong & Spivak, *Seven Sketches in Compositionality* §1.2.1, printed p. 8 (PDF p. 20), item `7sketches:1.2.1:def-setops` — union and intersection of subsets of a common set, the indexed union/intersection of a family indexed by the naturals, and the product and disjoint union of two sets. The product and disjoint-union clauses are already in-tree with their full universal properties, in two models, one of them computing (`Instance/Sets/Cartesian.v:32`, `Instance/Sets/Cocartesian.v:28` — whose cross-summand `False` IS the book's tagging — `Instance/FinSet/Product.v:105`, `Instance/FinSet.v:250`). The union/intersection clauses are this issue's obligation and are absent in every form: `rg -i 'union'` finds only DISJOINT unions, `Instance/FinSet/Pushout.v`'s union-find labelling and `Lib/FMapExt.v:821`'s map update, while `rg -i 'intersect'` finds only prose (`Structure/Pullback.v:94` calls a pullback of subobjects "the intersection" without defining it). `Coq.Sets.Ensembles` is imported by `Instance/Ens.v` and `Instance/Rel.v` but its `Union`/`Intersection`/`Included` are never used.

- [ ] (from Seven Sketches §1.2.1) the indexed union of a countably indexed family of subobjects (the issue's wide-pullback plan covers indexed INTERSECTIONS; the indexed JOIN is the missing dual), with the book's worked case: the union of the increasing family `∅, {1}, {1,2}, …` is the positive naturals and its intersection is empty
- [ ] (from Seven Sketches §1.2.1) the unit law `∅ ∪ X ≅ X` at the level of subobjects (currently only the dual coproduct form `coprod_zero_l` at `Structure/Cocartesian.v:375` exists)

### Also covered by

Fong & Spivak, *Seven Sketches in Compositionality* §1.2.1, printed p. 8 (PDF p. 20), item `7sketches:1.2.1:ex11` — an enumeration exercise contrasting the DISJOINT union of two sets (five elements, tagged) with their ordinary union inside a common ambient set (four elements, merged). Its parts (2) and (5) are the union half of this issue; its parts (1), (3), (4) are arithmetic that is definitional in skeletal FinSet but never evaluated at these instances (`Instance/FinSet/Topos.v` asserts only `Pow 2 = 4` at `:52` and `Pow 0 = 1` at `:54`, and no Example computes `2 × 3` or `2 + 3` at the object level).

- [ ] (from Seven Sketches §1.2.1) the merging-versus-tagging contrast made concrete: for two subobjects of one finite ambient object, the union has four elements where the coproduct has five
- [ ] (from Seven Sketches §1.2.1) the concrete FinSet evaluations `Pow 3 = 8`, `2 × 3 = 6` and `2 + 3 = 5` recorded as `eq_refl` Examples, and the elements of a small power object enumerated (the `fin_tabulate`/`fin_apply` codec elements are never listed)

### Also covered by

Fong & Spivak, *Seven Sketches in Compositionality* §1.2.1, printed p. 10 (PDF p. 22), item `7sketches:1.2.1:def21` — the quotient of a set by an equivalence relation, defined as the SET OF PARTS of the corresponding partition. The library's quotient discipline is the setoid one — a quotient is another choice of `≈` on the same carrier, stated as design at `Instance/Sets.v:66` and `Theory/Category.v:93` — and the only class-based quotient is per-instance: `Instance/FinSet/Pushout.v:406`'s `po_apex` counts the classes, `:420`'s `po_cls` is the quotient map and `:445`'s `po_cls_rep` exhibits a representative, all for the pushout-generated relation only. There is no operator taking a `SetoidObject` and an equivalence relation on its carrier to `A/R`. Note the same-name trap: `Construction/Quotient.v:254`'s `Quotient` is a quotient of a CATEGORY by a hom-congruence (identity on objects, `HomRel` Prop-valued at `:221`), and `Structure/Regular.v:71`'s `regular_coeq` gives coequalizers only of kernel pairs.

- [ ] (from Seven Sketches §1.2.1) a general quotient operator `A/R` for a `SetoidObject` `A` and an equivalence relation `R` on its carrier coarser than `≈`, with its quotient map and universal property in `Sets`
- [ ] (from Seven Sketches §1.2.1) the class-based presentation the book actually gives — the quotient as the set of PARTS of the corresponding partition — proved isomorphic to the setoid-coarsening presentation

### Also covered by

Fong & Spivak, *Seven Sketches in Compositionality* §1.2.1, printed p. 11 (PDF p. 23), item `7sketches:1.2.1:ex25` — a set admitting a function to the empty set is itself empty, i.e. the initial object is STRICT. `rg -in 'strict initial|strictly initial'` = 0 hits, and no lemma of shape `(x ~> 0) → x ≅ 0` exists: `Structure/Initial.v` (`initial_obj`:106, `zero`:109, `zero_unique`:112, `zero_comp`:124) constrains only maps OUT OF `0`, and none of the concrete initial objects (`Instance/Sets.v:265`, `Instance/Coq.v:187`, `Instance/FinSet.v:223`, `Instance/Rel.v:90`, `Instance/Props.v:61`) says anything about strictness. The ingredients are two lines away — `Structure/BiCCC.v:208`'s annihilation `prod_zero_l : 0 × x ≅ 0` together with `zero_unique` gives it — but the implication is never drawn.

- [ ] (from Seven Sketches §1.2.1) strict initiality: any object admitting a morphism into the initial object is isomorphic to it, derived from `Structure/BiCCC.v:208`'s annihilation and `Structure/Initial.v:112`'s `zero_unique`, and instantiated at `Sets`/`FinSet`

### Also covered by

Fong & Spivak, *Seven Sketches in Compositionality* §1.2.2, printed p. 13 (PDF p. 25), item `7sketches:1.2.2:remark31` — a preorder is exactly an equivalence relation with symmetry dropped. Both endpoints are in-tree in precisely the axiom shapes the remark compares, over a SHARED vocabulary (`PreOrder` and `Equivalence` both come from `Coq.Classes.RelationClasses` and are built from the same `Reflexive`/`Symmetric`/`Transitive` classes): `Theory/Category.v:282`'s `hom_preorder` asserts the two axioms, and `Lib/Setoid.v:32`'s `Setoid` carries the three. The comparison itself is unformalised — no `Equivalence R → PreOrder R`, no `PreOrder R → Symmetric R → Equivalence R`, and no thin-groupoid counterpart to `Construction/Enriched/Two.v:165`'s preorder characterisation.

- [ ] (from Seven Sketches §1.2.2) the two-way axiom comparison: every `Equivalence` is a `PreOrder`, and a `PreOrder` that is `Symmetric` is an `Equivalence` — stated so that "a preorder is an equivalence relation minus symmetry" is an in-tree fact

### Also covered by

Fong & Spivak, *Seven Sketches in Compositionality* §1.2.2, printed p. 13 (PDF p. 25), item `7sketches:1.2.2:example33` — the codiscrete (indiscrete) preorder on a set, in which every pair is related both ways. It is the companion of the discrete preorder this issue's correspondence already covers, and it is absent: `rg -in 'codiscrete|indiscrete|chaotic'` finds only prose pointers (`Structure/Discrete.v:23-24` names "the dual (codiscrete / indiscrete) construction" without building it, `Instance/StrictCat/Funny.v:40-42` names the chaotic groupoid as a counterexample without building it), and the only constantly-inhabited hom in the tree is `Instance/One.v:27`'s terminal category, where discrete and codiscrete coincide. `Theory/Bicategory/Lax.v:171-172` builds a codiscrete SETOID on `unit`, not a preorder on a general set.

- [ ] (from Seven Sketches §1.2.2) the codiscrete preorder on an arbitrary set, built as a `Proset` alongside the discrete one, with the observation that it is the terminal preorder structure on that carrier

### Also covered by

Fong & Spivak, *Seven Sketches in Compositionality* §1.2.2, printed p. 15 (PDF p. 27), item `7sketches:1.2.2:remark43` — total orders, introduced through the notion of two elements being COMPARABLE: a total order is a preorder in which every two elements are comparable. The `TotalOrder` structure is already this issue's obligation; the comparability predicate it is phrased through is not broken out anywhere, and nothing in the tree defines it (`rg -i 'comparab'` finds one hit, the English word "INCOMPARABLE" at `Structure/Monoidal/CopyDiscard.v:42`). The near miss to reject is `Construction/Enriched/Two.v:65`'s `tpre_dec`, which is DECIDABILITY of the order — satisfied by the maximally non-total discrete preorder — not totality.

- [ ] (from Seven Sketches §1.2.2) a named `comparable x y := (x ≤ y) + (y ≤ x)` predicate, with `TotalOrder` characterised as "every two elements are comparable", and a header note distinguishing it from `tpre_dec`-style decidability

### Also covered by

Fong & Spivak, *Seven Sketches in Compositionality* §1.2.2, printed p. 15 (PDF p. 27), item `7sketches:1.2.2:ex44` — the exercise asks whether a discrete preorder is one in which NO two elements are comparable, the catch being reflexivity. Both facts it turns on are in-tree: `Instance/Discrete.v:65`'s `DiscreteCat_Discrete` gives `x ≤ y → x = y`, and `Theory/Category.v:282`'s `hom_preorder` (whose `PreOrder_Reflexive := fun _ => id`, realised at `Instance/Discrete.v:41` as `id := eq_refl`) is the reflexivity catch. Only the vocabulary is missing, so the exercise's sentence cannot be stated or corrected in-tree.

- [ ] (from Seven Sketches §1.2.2) the corrected statement, once comparability exists: in a discrete preorder every element is comparable with itself and DISTINCT elements are incomparable — the contrapositive of `DiscreteCat_Discrete` recorded as a statement about comparability

### Also covered by

Fong & Spivak, *Seven Sketches in Compositionality* §1.2.2, printed p. 15 (PDF p. 27), item `7sketches:1.2.2:example45` — the naturals with their usual order form a TOTAL order (hence a linear diagram), contrasted with the branching partition order; the example then lists three further orders on the same carrier. This is a multi-part item: its totality clause belongs here, and its divisibility clause is filed separately as its own Seven Sketches issue. Three of the four orders are in-tree — the usual one three times over (`Instance/Proset.v:47`, `Instance/Poset.v:120`, `Test/Poset.v:54`, plus the Type-valued twin `Instance/Omega.v:28`), the discrete one (`Instance/Discrete.v:65`), and the reverse only as the general `C^op` (`Construction/Opposite.v:106`, never applied to the naturals) — while totality is stated for no order at all.

- [ ] (from Seven Sketches §1.2.2) the naturals proved to be a `TotalOrder` instance, and the reverse order exhibited concretely as `(ℕ, ≤)^op` rather than only as the general opposite construction

### Also covered by

Fong & Spivak, *Seven Sketches in Compositionality* §1.3.1, printed p. 25 (PDF p. 37), item `7sketches:1.3.1:example89` — in a total order the meet of a subset is its infimum and the join its supremum, which generalises the boolean case. Both halves are currently unavailable: totality is this issue's obligation, and `rg -i 'infimum|supremum|greatest lower|least upper|glb|lub'` returns 0 statements tree-wide (the sole hit is the comment at `Instance/Poset.v:51`, "the limit over a subset is its greatest lower bound"). The categorical half — that a limit of a discrete diagram in a thin category IS the meet — is #737's identification lemma, so this increment is the naming and the total-order specialisation.

- [ ] (from Seven Sketches §1.3.1) infimum/supremum introduced as the order-theoretic names, and proved to coincide with the discrete-diagram meet/join in a `TotalOrder` (specialising #737's identification lemma), with the two-element order as the worked instance

### Also covered by

Fong & Spivak, *Seven Sketches in Compositionality* §1.2.2, printed p. 13 (PDF p. 25), item `7sketches:1.2.2:remark35` — a partial order is a preorder satisfying `x ≅ y → x = y`, which in categorical language is SKELETALITY, so partial orders are exactly the skeletal preorders. This is a multi-part item; its posetal-reflection clause is recorded against #372. The definitional half is in-tree and even glossed in prose — `Instance/Poset.v:116` defines a poset as a `Proset` plus `@Antisymmetric`, and its header at `:19-22` says antisymmetry "only makes the resulting thin category skeletal, so that isomorphic objects are equal", citing nLab — but there is no `Skeletal` predicate for an arbitrary category (`rg -E 'Class Skeletal|Definition Skeletal|Record Skeletal'` = 0 hits), so the identification cannot be stated, only exemplified: the skeletality assertions exist ONLY in the regression-guard file `Test/Poset.v` (`poset_nat_skeletal`:102, `poset_two_skeletal`:150), never in the library proper. `Structure/Discrete.v`'s `Discrete` is discreteness, strictly stronger than skeletality.

- [ ] (from Seven Sketches §1.2.2) "partial orders are exactly the skeletal preorders" stated and proved with the general `Skeletal` predicate, relating it to the `@Antisymmetric` hypothesis of `Instance/Poset.v:116`, so the fact leaves `Test/Poset.v` and enters the library proper

### Also covered by

Fong & Spivak, *Seven Sketches in Compositionality* §1.2.2, printed p. 13 (PDF p. 25), item `7sketches:1.2.2:remark35` — the second half of the remark: the preorder/partial-order distinction is inessential, because every preorder becomes a partial order by identifying mutually related elements. That posetal reflection is exactly this issue's obligation and has no in-tree counterpart: `rg -iE 'posetal reflection|poset reflection|quotient of a preorder|identify equivalent'` = 0 hits, and `Theory/Equivalence.v:92-99` explicitly records that the library "confines skeletons to concrete instances". `Construction/Quotient.v:254`'s `Quotient` quotients a category by a hom-congruence and is identity-on-objects, so it cannot identify OBJECTS and is not the required construction. (The remark's skeletality clause is recorded against #374.)

- [ ] (from Seven Sketches §1.2.2) the two illustrations the remark draws from the reflection: a discrete preorder is already a partial order (available from `Instance/Discrete.v:65`), and a codiscrete preorder reflects to the unique partial order on a one-element set

### Also covered by

Fong & Spivak, *Seven Sketches in Compositionality* §1.2.2, printed p. 14 (PDF p. 26), item `7sketches:1.2.2:example37` — a displayed four-vertex, five-arrow graph whose path counts are read off: exactly one path between one pair, none between another, exactly the length-zero path from a vertex to itself, and INFINITELY MANY between two vertices because of a loop. This is the same obligation as this issue's hom-counting for concrete graphs, extended to a graph with a loop. In-tree there is no concrete multi-vertex quiver at all: `Build_Quiver_Standard_Eq` has exactly two occurrences, its definition at `Construction/Free/Quiver.v:194` and its single use at `Test/Issue138.v:87` (one node, one loop), whose only assertions are `Check (FreeOnQuiver B138_loop : Category)` at `:90` and `Example B138_free_loop_nodes … = Datatypes.unit := eq_refl` at `:95` — nothing describes, counts or bounds any hom-set, so even that loop's infinitely many paths are never stated. `tlist_length` hits (`Lib/TList.v:81`, `Construction/Free/Quiver.v:114`) are structural and count nothing between two vertices.

- [ ] (from Seven Sketches §1.2.2) a concrete four-vertex, five-arrow quiver including a LOOP, with its hom-sets described: the empty, singleton and length-zero cases settled and the loop's hom-set shown infinite (equivalently, in bijection with the naturals)

### Also covered by

Fong & Spivak, *Seven Sketches in Compositionality* §1.2.2, printed p. 14 (PDF p. 26), item `7sketches:1.2.2:ex38` — complete the source/target table of the displayed graph, i.e. present a concrete graph by its two structure functions. This bears on how a graph is presented in-tree: `Construction/Free/Quiver.v:54`'s `edges : nodes → nodes → uedges` indexes edges BY their endpoints, so no source and target functions exist as data to tabulate; the one place they are honest functions is `Instance/Parallel.v:166`'s `Presheaf_Graph` (`source := fst`, `target := snd`), a different, fully specified infinite graph. `Construction/Free/Quiver.v:398`'s `QuiverOfCat` likewise leaves endpoints implicit.

- [ ] (from Seven Sketches §1.2.2) the source/target presentation of a graph related to the endpoint-indexed `edges` presentation of `Construction/Free/Quiver.v:54` — a conversion in both directions — so that a graph given by two functions (as the book gives it) can be fed to `FreeOnQuiver`

### Also covered by

Fong & Spivak, *Seven Sketches in Compositionality* §1.2.2, printed p. 16 (PDF p. 28), item `7sketches:1.2.2:example50` — the power set of a set ordered by inclusion, this being the order always intended when a power set is regarded as an ordered set. Building that thin category is exactly this issue's item 1. Two in-tree remarks worth carrying: `Structure/SubobjectClassifier.v:187`'s `classifier_classifies` is an isomorphism of SETOIDS and is order-forgetting, and no internal `⊆ : Pow a × Pow a ~> Ω` is defined on `Structure/Topos.v:129`'s `Pow a := Ω ^ a`; and the trap the issue already names is real — `Instance/Ens.v:56`'s `EnsT T` does have all subsets of a fixed carrier as objects, but its homs are `∃ f : T → T, ∀ x, x ∈ A ↔ x ∈ f⁻¹ B`, so at `f := id` they force extensional equality, not inclusion.

- [ ] (from Seven Sketches §1.2.2) the external inclusion order transported to the power OBJECT: an internal `⊆ : Pow a × Pow a ~> Ω` compatible with `classifier_classifies`, so that "the power set regarded as an ordered set" holds at `Pow a` and not only at `SubObj a`

### Also covered by

Fong & Spivak, *Seven Sketches in Compositionality* §1.2.2, printed p. 16 (PDF p. 28), item `7sketches:1.2.2:ex51` — the inclusion orders on the power sets of the empty, one-element and two-element sets (one, two and four elements respectively). The order is this issue's obligation; the counts are partly in-tree and reduce by `eq_refl` through a real exponential codec, but only two of the three cases are recorded: `Instance/FinSet/Topos.v:54` (`Pow 0 = 1`) and `:52` (`Pow 2 = 4`). `Pow 1 = 2` appears nowhere, and `rg -n 'FinSet_Pow'` confirms there is no third computation beyond `FinSet_Pow_membership` at `:89`.

- [ ] (from Seven Sketches §1.2.2) `Pow 1 = 2` recorded as an `eq_refl` Example, completing the family in `Instance/FinSet/Topos.v`
- [ ] (from Seven Sketches §1.2.2) the inclusion order exhibited on each of the three small power sets — the single arrow on the two-element case and the square on the four-element case — so that the power sets are distinguished from arbitrary sets of the same size

### Also covered by

Fong & Spivak, *Seven Sketches in Compositionality* §1.4.3, printed p. 32 (PDF pp. 44–45), item `7sketches:1.4.3:example117` — the "apples and buckets" example: for a function between sets the preimage map on power sets has BOTH adjoints, the left one being the direct image and the right one the dual image. The preimage/direct-image adjunction is exactly this issue's central deliverable; this is a multi-part item and its dual-image leg is recorded against #384, as this issue's body already anticipates. Current state on the one leg that does exist: `Theory/Subobject/Functor.v:180`'s `Sub : C^op ⟶ Sets` (with `sub_reindex` at `:35` and `sub_reindex_respects` at `:60`) is a faithful and more general preimage, but it lands in `Sets` and is functorial for `≈` only — `sub_le` has 0 occurrences in that file, so MONOTONICITY of the preimage for the subobject order is nowhere stated. The direct image exists only as the image of a WHOLE morphism (`Instance/Sets/Image.v:75`, `:143`), never as an operation `SubObj A → SubObj B`; the only in-tree use of `Sets_Image` as a subobject is `Instance/Sets/Classifier.v:341`'s `sets_char_subobject`, which merely identifies a mono with its own image.

- [ ] (from Seven Sketches §1.4.3) the direct image as an OPERATION on subobjects, `f_! : SubObj A → SubObj B`, assembled from `Instance/Sets/Image.v:75` — currently only whole-morphism images exist
- [ ] (from Seven Sketches §1.4.3) monotonicity of the preimage for the subobject order, `sub_le u v → sub_le (sub_reindex f u) (sub_reindex f v)` (only the weaker `Proper (equiv ==> equiv)` is proved today)

### Also covered by

Fong & Spivak, *Seven Sketches in Compositionality* §1.4.3, printed p. 32 (PDF pp. 44–45), item `7sketches:1.4.3:example117` — the third leg of the "apples and buckets" adjoint triple: the dual (universal) image, `f_*(A') = {b | every element of the fibre over b lies in A'}` (empty fibres counting vacuously), right adjoint to the preimage. This is the universal quantifier of the substitution adjoint triple, hence this issue's obligation; the direct-image/preimage legs are recorded against #382. In-tree the dual image has no counterpart whatsoever at any level: `rg -in 'dual image|universal image'` = 0 hits, and `Theory/Subobject/Functor.v`'s reindexing has no adjoint on either side (`sub_reindex`'s only consumer outside its own file is `Structure/SubobjectClassifier.v`, which uses it for the classification bijection, not for an adjoint).

- [ ] (from Seven Sketches §1.4.3) the dual image `f_*` on subsets/subobjects with the biconditional `f*(B') ⊆ A' ⟺ B' ⊆ f_*(A')`, presented in the book's elementwise form (buckets all of whose apples are chosen, empty buckets vacuously included) alongside the quantifier reading

### Also covered by

Fong & Spivak, *Seven Sketches in Compositionality* §1.4.3, printed p. 33 (PDF p. 45), item `7sketches:1.4.3:ex118` — compute the preimage, the direct image and the dual image on chosen subsets of small finite sets. ### Also covered by

Fong & Spivak, *Seven Sketches in Compositionality* §1.2.2, printed p. 17 (PDF p. 29), item `7sketches:1.2.2:example54` — the UPPER sets of a preorder (subsets closed upward) and the preorder they form under inclusion, worked out for the two-element order (three upper sets: `∅`, `{true}`, everything, linearly ordered, with `{false}` excluded). This is the dual of this issue's lower-set poset — mathematically the lower sets of the opposite preorder — and the whole of Seven Sketches Chapter 1 is phrased in the upper-set direction, so the dual needs to be reachable rather than merely implied. Current state: `rg -in 'upper'` over all `*.v` returns exactly four hits, all unrelated geometry prose (`Structure/Regular.v:101`, `:126`; `Structure/Monoidal/Collapse.v:255`; `Structure/Monoidal/Braided.v:38`); `rg -in 'up-set|upset|upclosed|upward.?closed|Alexandrov|down.set|lower set|order.ideal'` = 0; `rg -in 'sieve'` gives 2 prose hits only; `rg -n 'Included'` = 0.

- [ ] (from Seven Sketches §1.2.2) the UPPER-set poset `Up(P)` made available as well as `Low(P)` — either as a definition in its own right or as `Low(P^op)` with the identification proved — and the two-element order's three upper sets computed, with `{false}` refuted as an upper set

### Also covered by

Fong & Spivak, *Seven Sketches in Compositionality* §1.2.2, printed p. 17 (PDF p. 29), item `7sketches:1.2.2:ex55` — for the DISCRETE preorder on a set, the preorder of upper sets is exactly the power set ordered by inclusion, since every subset is upward closed when the order is equality. Both sides of the asserted equality are currently missing: upper/lower sets are this issue's obligation, and the power set as an ORDER is #382's (`rg -n 'Included'` = 0; `Structure/Topos.v:129`'s `Pow a := Ω ^ a` carries no order; `Instance/Ens.v:56`'s `EnsT T` is ordered by membership-preserving-and-reflecting endofunctions, not inclusion). The discrete side is ready: `Instance/Discrete.v:37`'s `DiscreteCat` (`hom := fun x y => x = y`) with `DiscreteCat_Discrete` at `:65`.
